short: Audio memory recall (M02) is ahead as a design, but the LRW state-of-the-art claim misses a prior 87.9% model, the edge over distillation is one run, and GRID gains are small.
position: The paper [@kim2021multimodality] stores audio features in a memory during training and recalls them from video at test (M02), feeding them ahead of the backend (M06). The recall design is ahead: no earlier study among 54 on audio-to-video knowledge transfer records it (pattern match), and its gain over a no-memory baseline repeats on LRW and LRW-1000; its edge over distillation is one LRW run of 0.91 points. The LRW state-of-the-art claim fails: 85.41% is 2.5 points below an uncited earlier single model at 87.9% [@ma2021towards]; on public LRW-1000, 50.82% leads earlier models without word-boundary input by 2.8 points but not the 55.7% reached with boundaries [@feng2020learn]. Every headline number is the best memory size of an ablation, from one run. On GRID the objective lead over Lip2Wav is 0.007 STOI with no no-memory score in the main text, and the opinion-score jump comes from swapping in WaveNet.
